newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England makes no move on interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England makes no move on interest rates.

text.p: The Bank of England signalled no change in official interest rates on Wednesday after the monthly monetary policy meeting between finance minister Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
The Bank engaged in routine money market operations at 1400 GMT at unchanged dealing rates, indicating that official interest rates remain at 6.0 percent.
However, economists said the possibility that official rates might be adjusted on Thursday morning could not be ruled out.

The central bank normally does not change interest rates on the same day as a monetary meeting if it has already operated at existing rates in the money market, as appeared to be the case on Wednesday.

The uncertainty about whether a move might have been deferred means traders will be glued to their screens on Thursday morning, when the Bank announces its forecast of the daily liquidity shortage and conducts any required operations.
Clarke, who has the final say on monetary policy, raised rates unexpectedly by a quarter-point to 6.0 percent on October 30.

The Bank has since warned that rates will have to rise again to ward off an upsurge in inflation as economic recovery gathers momentum, but George said last week there was no urgent need for another increase.
A Reuters poll of 21 economists showed none expected a rate increase this month.
However, financial markets do expect monetary policy to be tightened again early in the new year.
